Highlights
This release features 762 commits from 315 contributors (104 new)!
New models: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (#56214, #56228, #56208) with the whole KV stored in MXFP8 through the FlashMLA V4.1 record on SM100 (#56893), DeepGEMM Mega-mHC (#56962), and async Engram prefetch with Engram DP sharding (#56512); DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (#54566), also on ROCm (#55107) and with LoRA (#55897); GLM-5.3-Flash (#53906) with EPLB (#55119); K2-Horizon (#55063); Cohere Compass (#54774); Bailing V3 VL (#55921); Nanbeige4.2 via the Transformers backend (#56071); and a DeepSeek-V4 CPU backend with AVX512/AMX sparse MLA, indexer, mHC and compressor kernels (#55355).
Fast Start: a persistent per-GPU weight-cache daemon holds post-quantized, TP-sharded weights in GPU memory so restarting engines map them over CUDA IPC with --load-format ipccache instead of reloading from disk (#54921), now covering FP4 checkpoints (#55465) and multi-node TP (#55468).

data.author: khluu

Highlights
This release features 717 commits from 307 contributors (96 new)!
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash performance: FlashMLA mega attention with the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV cache is now the SM100 default (#56935); DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits for the indexer (#56254) and Mega-Gate fusing the gate GEMM with expert selection (#56266); decoder boundaries fuse the TP all-reduce, mHC input preparation (#57643) and the MoE finalize (#58586); a fused small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103 (#58634); the MXFP8 wob GEMM fused with the sequence-parallel reduce-scatter (#57428); Engram wkv sharded across TP ranks (#58678) and Engram host tables shared across co-located DP replicas by default (#57651); encoder CUDA graphs for the vision tower (#56625); and SWA bounded replay that keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching (#56227).

data.author: khluu
data.summary:
v0.33.0
Highlights
This release features 927 commits from 389 contributors (122 new)!
New models: Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) with its DFlash2 drafter (#62074), Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (#57963), Recursive Flint (40B MoE, 2.5B active) (#62938), Muse Spark Open (#61879), Step-5 Preview (#61727, #63147), NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (#62957), Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (#60149), Nemotron Parse 3.5 (#61651), MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (#63095), Domyn Edge (#62544) and the ColUltraVBERT visual document retriever (#62237).
PyTorch 2.14: vLLM is upgraded to PyTorch 2.14.0, with torchvision 0.29.0 and Triton 3.8.0 (#52183).
CUDA 12.9 dropped: release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only. The CUDA 12.9 wheels and the -cu129 / -cu129-ubuntu2404 images are no longer published (#62575); use the default CUDA 13.0 artifacts instead.
libtorch ABI stable CUDA wheel: the CUDA wheel is now ABI stable with libtorch.
AWS EFA image: a new vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa image (x8664 and aarch64) bundles the AWS EFA libraries and the EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine, for KV transfer and multi-node serving on EFA-enabled EC2 instances (#58768).
vllm/vllm image alias: every release image is now also published under the shorter vllm/vllm name, e.g. vllm/vllm:v0.33.0, vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa and vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm.
Speculative decoding: the new XPress refiner for block-diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark (#54448); FLy, an opt-in lossy verification policy with 1.04-1.31x decode throughput on MI355X and B300 (#53987); DFlash/DSpark no longer reserve draft slots in the token budget, taking DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300 from 1373 to 3390 output tok/s in the PR's benchmark (#59468); quantized draft lmhead (draftlmheadquantization, +18% decode at concurrency 1) (#59973); lookahead block hashes so EAGLE/MTP prefix-cache hits keep their last block, on by default (#61589); and MTP drafts in the Transformers modeling backend (#61270).

data.title: huggingface/transformers v5.22.0: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
data.author: LysandreJik
data.summary:
New Models
Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.
Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.
Key Features
Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:
1T total / 52B active parameters: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
1M context length, for long-context workloads.
Multimodal input: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
Instruct and Reasoning functionalities with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.
Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:
Reasoning Mode: three reasoning efforts — low, medium, high (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
Vision: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
Multilingual: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
System Prompt: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
Agentic: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.
Cybersecurity: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests.

data.title: vllm-project/vllm v0.32.0
data.author: khluu
data.summary:
v0.32.0
Highlights
This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!
Structured decisions and generic parsers: the new POST /v1/systemone endpoint answers choice, noul and score questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064), LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new hf tool and reasoning parser (--tool-call-parser hf, --reasoning-parser hf) reads the checkpoint's responsetemplate, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
Low-precision KV cache everywhere: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); fp8dsmla on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit ultraquant4bit KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
Model Runner V2: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
Faster startup and serving: vllm download-kernels installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); vllm preload --preload-autotune keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with --api-server-count above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in th

data.title: open-webui/open-webui v0.13.1
data.author: github-actions[bot]
data.summary:
Added
🦾 Coding agents as models. On an Open Terminal that offers agents, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi now appear in the model picker. You can chat with them or call them by voice, choose their reasoning effort and service tier, and approve their tool requests in the chat. Each conversation uses one agent, and agent chats cannot be regenerated, continued or edited and resent. If an agent's terminal goes away, its chats and new chats fall back to the default model and earlier replies keep the agent's name. Autocompletion in agent chats uses the task model, or is skipped when there is none. #33843, #33860, #33880, #33857
🪢 Introducing Tether. Tether is the new desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that ties your own computer to Open WebUI. Sign in once and your computer shows up under Your devices in the terminal menu, so models, coding agents and automations can work in your real files, repositories and tools, and you can reach them from any browser, including your phone. Tether connects out to Open WebUI, so there are no ports to open, its terminal output resumes after a dropped connection, and it delivers notifications to your desktop even when no Open WebUI page is open. It signs in with a renewable session that expires after 90 days without use by default, set with "SESSIONEXPIRESIN".
💸 Much cheaper tool chats. Chats that use tools now cost much less. Citation instructions, memory recall, the skills list and attached knowledge are no longer rewritten into the system prompt or your message on every tool round, so the start of the conversation stays the same between requests and providers can serve it from their prompt cache. Custom pipes see a different message layout as a result; see Context as hidden tool results under Changed. #33852

data.author: github-actions[bot]
data.summary:
Blog post: https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/llama-cpp-v1
Overview
llama.cpp v1.0.0 removes the deprecated public API and promotes the NextN/speculative API to llama.h, adds OCP FP8 KV caches, a host-memory MoE expert cache with a configurable CPU share, and loading of external PLE shards. It adds three text architectures (Kimi-K3.1-Pro, Ripple and xing40), drama-3 TTS, and MageVL-Cowork and Kimi-K3.1 vision, hardens llama-server (SSRF, CORS, DNS rebinding, MCP tool cancellation) and adds a /v1/audio/speech endpoint, ships a redesigned web UI with chat groups and a markdown editor, and updates ggml to v1.0.0.

data.title: huggingface/transformers Release v5.23.0
data.author: vasqu
data.summary:
Release v5.23.0
New Model additions
Inkling2
Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch.
Links: Documentation | Blog Post
Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in #50682
JEV
JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. JevForDecision is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (head.safetensors and judgeconfig.json for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental decision pipeline or directly with decide.
Note: JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments.
Links: Documentation
Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in #50054
LFM3
LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-window layers. data.title: vllm-project/vllm v0.34.0
data.author: khluu
data.summary:
v0.34.0
1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new). Thank you!
TL;DR
10 new models (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!)
Extensible KV cache is on by default: vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now remove gpumemoryutilization from your configs.
Model Runner V1 is gone. Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner.
Big speedups on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3).
Upgrade check: default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and huggingfacehub >= 2.0.0 is required. See Before you upgrade.
Before you upgrade
> [!IMPORTANT]
> These changes can break existing setups.
| Change | What to do | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model Runner V1 removed | Remove VLLMUSEV2MODELRUNNER=0; it now fails at startup. Port V1 logits processors to vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logitsprocessor. | #63373 |
| Default --block-size is 64 (was 16) | Pass --block-size 16 to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16. | #63231 |
| Extensible KV cache on by default; gpumemoryutilization defaults to 1.0 | In most cases it's now best to not set gpumemoryutilization. This should provide maximum kv cache capacity while avoiding runtime OOMs. Use it to share a GPU with other processes or when extensible kv cache is disabled. | #56492 |
| ROCm 7.2 artifacts dropped | Use the ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. -rocm72 is no longer published. | #61939 |
| huggingfacehub >= 2.0.0 required | Also requires tokenizers >= 0.23.3 and timm >= 1.0.30. | #64779 |
| QuTLASS / fpquant removed | fpquant checkpoints no longer load. | #65230 |
| Marlin W4A8 removed | Use --quantization humming with VLLMHUMMINGINPUTQUANTCONFIG instead of VLLMMARLININPUTDTYPE. | #65542 |
| Keye-VL and Keye-VL-1.5 removed | — | #64287 |
All breaking changes, deprecations and new defaults

data.title: open-webui/open-webui v0.13.4
data.author: github-actions[bot]
data.summary:
Added
Bring your own computer with Tether. Tether turns your own computer into part of Open WebUI: models from Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server, OpenAPI and MCP tool servers and Open Terminal servers that you add in the Tether app now show up just for you in the model selector, the Tools list of the + menu and the terminal menu of any Open WebUI you connect, from whatever device you open it on, and Open WebUI reaches them through Tether, so their addresses, commands and keys never leave your computer. This needs Tether 0.1.14 or later, or 0.1.16 for MCP servers, tool servers and terminals need "ENABLETOOLSERVERS" turned on, and a Tether model whose ID matches a model already in Open WebUI stays hidden. Tether replaces Direct Connections. #34397
Sandboxed agents on your own computer. Tether 0.1.13 or later can lock the terminal on your computer into a sandbox, so models and coding agents work in your real files without reaching the rest of your machine: on macOS and supported Windows devices, Open Terminal and everything it launches, coding agents included, can only touch the one folder you pick, run offline unless you turn on Network access and accept no incoming connections, with no Docker, virtual machine or administrator setup needed. If the sandbox cannot be enforced, the terminal stays stopped instead of quietly running without it, and browser and desktop control stay off while it is on. Turn it on in Tether under Settings > Open Terminal > Sandbox.
Local MCP servers through Tether. Open WebUI can now use MCP servers that run as a local command over stdio, the way many MCP servers are distributed, by launching them on your computer through Tether 0.1.16 or later, with no proxy such as mcpo and no port to open. Add one in Tether under Settings > Integrations > Tools with its command, or connect an MCP server by its web address, and pick it from the Tools list of the + menu. Local commands run with your own account's access, outside Tether's work
